rationale: The six core refs each bind a current measurable loss or paid event, an identifiable operating or compliance budget, and a bounded route to contractual control: recurring supplier-evidence custody (mf-03), dealer intake certification (mf-08), a building charging concession (mf-11), building-wide loss-prevention telemetry and dispatch (mf-12), installer-fed failed-unit exchange (fb-11), and owner-mandated equipment-data access (ws-08). The founder's installer channel directly strengthens four of those routes, while the other two can begin through narrow broker or dealer contracts within the capital and time bounds. The wildcards preserve asymmetric structures not copied from core: sponsor-funded validation that could create reusable consented benchmark data (fb-07), and an owned-or-leased reusable-packaging clearing ring whose economics depend on route density (ws-07). Calibration treated wording and industry swaps as non-novel, including the recovered-refrigerant pair, the waste-heat-option pair, and neighboring flexibility, regulatory-evidence, battery-attestation, grid-option, and repair-inventory families. Delayed history was used to exclude renamed slot-recovery, white-certificate, generic site-option, authorized-representative, and micropollutant-allocation repetitions rather than to penalize missing present evidence. No defensible observed missing-archetype claim is made.
